column2: One day at night the elder, taking a knife, cut the limbs of the son as he slept beside his bride.
That night she hacked every limb of Ghushma's son; then, proud and strong, she carried him off and threw him into the lake,
there where Ghushma daily cast her lingas. Having thrown him in, she came back content and slept at ease.
Rising at dawn, Ghushma did her daily worship as always, and the excellent Sudharma himself performed his daily rites.
Meanwhile the elder went about the household work full of joy, the fire in her heart now quieted.
Everyone constantly praised her for bearing a son; the elder could not bear it, nor the child's beauty and the rest.
Rising at dawn, the bride looked at the bed, saw it wet with blood and strewn with pieces of the body, and was stricken with grief.
She told her mother-in-law: "Where has your son gone? The bed is wet with blood, and pieces of his body are to be seen.
Alas, I am ruined! Who has done this wicked deed, O you of pure vows?" Saying this, his beloved wept bitterly in many ways.
The elder then made a show of grief, crying "Alas, I am ruined!"; outwardly she grieved, but in her mind she was full of delight.
Ghushma too, hearing her daughter-in-law's grief, did not waver from her vow of daily worship of the earthen linga.
Her mind was not the least bit agitated; her husband too remained so until the rite of the vow was complete.
At midday, at the end of the worship, she saw the dreadful bed; even then Ghushma showed no grief at all.

He who gave this son will himself protect him. He is famed as the lover of his devotees, the Death of Death, the refuge of the good.
shivpurana:8:33.28	If Shambhu, the one sole lord and master, does not protect us — like a garland-maker, he joins those he unites and parts them too —
shivpurana:8:33.29	what would my worrying achieve today? Reflecting on this truth, she did not grieve, for she had found steadfastness in Shiva.
Seeing that beloved son, a vessel of good qualities to his parents, her heart then burned like fire.
Taking the earthen lingas, calm in mind as before, she went to the shore of the lake uttering the names of Shambhu.
When she had cast the earthen lingas there and turned back, she saw her son, risen from the lake, standing on the bank.
The son said: "Come, mother, let me embrace you. I was dead and now I am alive, by the power of your merit and the grace of Shankara."
Suta said: Seeing her son alive, Ghushma his mother, O brahmins, was not elated, just as she had not grieved before.
At that moment Shiva swiftly appeared there in the form of light, and Mahesha, well pleased, spoke.
Shiva said: "I am pleased; ask a boon. This boy was killed by that wicked woman; I will kill her with my trident, O fair-faced one."
Suta said: Then Ghushma, bowing low to Shiva, chose her boon: "Lord, this Sudeha, my sister, must be protected by you."
Shiva said: "She has done you harm; how can you do her a kindness? Sudeha, the evil-doer, deserves to be killed."
Ghushma said: "At the mere sight of you no sin remains; now that she has seen you, that sin of hers will be reduced to ashes.
Whoever does good in return for harm — at the mere sight of such a one, sin goes far away.
Meanwhile brahmins came to give a girl in marriage, and he duly performed his son's wedding there.
So I have heard, O God, the wonderful word of the Lord; therefore, O Sadashiva, let it be done as such a one would do."
Suta said: Addressed thus by her, Maheshvara, ocean of compassion and fond of his devotees, was again greatly pleased and said to her:
Shiva said: "Ask another boon, Ghushma; I will grant what is good for you. I am well pleased by your devotion and your unperturbed nature."
Suta said: Hearing his words she said: "If a boon is to be given by you, O God, then for the protection of the worlds dwell here under my name."
Then Shiva, Maheshvara, well pleased, said: "I shall dwell here under your name as Ghushmesha, the giver of happiness.
Let my auspicious linga, renowned as Ghushmesha, come into being, and let this lake always be the abode of lingas.
Hence it shall be famed in the three worlds by the name Shivalaya; the very sight of this lake shall always grant every desire.
In your line, O woman of good vows, for a hundred and one generations such excellent sons will be born, without doubt —
with good wives, wealthy, long-lived and wise, learned and generous, attaining the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.
A hundred and one, abounding in virtue, will be born; such will be the splendid extension of your line."
Sudharma rejoiced greatly with Ghushma, and all the relatives paid honour to Ghushma.
Suta said: Having said this, Shiva became a linga there, famed by the name Ghushmesha, and the lake was known as Shivalaya.
Sudharma, Ghushma and Sudeha came together and quickly circumambulated Shiva a hundred and one times.
Having worshipped Mahesha and embraced one another, they cast off the impurity within and gained supreme happiness there.
Seeing the son alive, Sudeha was ashamed; having begged the two for forgiveness, O brahmins, she performed a vow that removes one's own sin.
Thus did this linga named Ghushmesha arise, O lords of sages; by seeing and worshipping it, happiness always grows.
Thus I have told you the series of the twelve jyotirlingas, which grant all desires and give enjoyment and liberation.
Whoever reads or hears this story of the jyotirlingas is freed from all sins and gains enjoyment and liberation.
Seeing him, Sudeha burned inwardly; she fell into extreme grief, saying, "Alas, I am ruined!"
Sudharma came home with the married son and his bride and showed his delight, as if to gladden both his dear wives.
Ghushma was delighted, but Sudeha fell into grief; unable to bear that happiness, she fell to the ground in anguish.
Ghushma said, "The bride and son are yours, not mine," and the bride and son lovingly regarded Sudeha as mother-in-law and mother.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, fourth book, the Kotirudra Samhita, chapter 34: the account of Vishnu's gaining of the Sudarshana discus. Vyasa said: Having heard these words of Suta, the lords of sages praised him highly and, desiring the good of the worlds, said to him:
Suta said: Addressed thus by the mighty Vishnu, all the gods, counting the wicked demons as already slain, went each to his own abode.
Vishnu too, for the victory of the immortals, worshipped Shiva, the ruler of all immortals, witness of all, the imperishable.
Going near Kailasa, Hari himself performed austerities, making a fire-pit and establishing the sacred fire before him.
With the rite of the earthen linga, with mantras of many kinds and with many hymns, he joyfully worshipped Girisha.
With lotuses grown in the lake called Manasa, O lords of sages, Hari took his seat there and did not stir.
I must stay here by all means until he grants his grace — having made this resolve, Hari worshipped Shiva.
When Hara still was not pleased with Hari, O brahmins, the blessed Vishnu became absorbed in reflection.
Reflecting thus in his mind, he rendered service in many ways, yet Hara, the lord who grants aid, was not pleased.
Then Vishnu, greatly astonished and filled with supreme devotion, lovingly praised the supreme lord with a thousand names.
Uttering a name-mantra for each lotus, he worshipped Shambhu, who is kind to those who seek refuge.
The sages said: "Suta, you know everything, so we ask you: tell us, lord, the greatness of the Harishvara linga.
Then, to test Vishnu's devotion, Shankara took away one lotus from the thousand.
Vishnu did not know of this wonderful working of maya; but realizing one was missing, he set about searching for it.
Firm in his vow, he wandered the whole earth to please him; not finding it, the pure-souled one plucked out one of his own eyes.
Seeing that, Shankara, remover of all sorrow, was pleased; he appeared right there and spoke to Hari.
Shiva said: "I am pleased with you, Hari; ask a boon as you wish. I will give what your mind desires; nothing is withheld from you."
Suta said: Hearing Shambhu's words, Keshava, delighted in mind and filled with great joy, spoke to Shiva with folded hands.
Vishnu said: "What need I say before you? You abide within as the inner controller. Still, lord, I speak out of respect for your command.
The world is oppressed by demons and we have no happiness, O Sadashiva; my own weapon, master, does not avail to slay the demons.
What shall I do, where shall I go? I have no other protector. Therefore, supreme lord, I have come to you for refuge."
Suta said: Having said this and bowed to Shiva, the supreme self, he stood before Shambhu, himself greatly afflicted.
We heard long ago that Vishnu obtained the Sudarshana discus by worshipping him; tell us that story in detail, dear one."
Suta said: Hearing these words of Vishnu, Maheshvara, god of gods, gave him his own discus Sudarshana, a mass of radiance.
Having obtained it, the blessed Vishnu swiftly slew all those mighty demons with that discus, without effort.
The world regained perfect well-being and the gods became happy; delighted at obtaining his weapon, Hari was greatly joyful.
The sages said: "What is that thousand names of Shankara? Tell us, since it was by that that Maheshvara, pleased, gave the discus to Hari.
Tell us its greatness together with Shiva's dialogue, and Shambhu's compassion toward Vishnu, just as it was."
Vyasa said: Hearing these words of the sages of cultivated minds, Suta, remembering the lotus feet of Shiva, spoke.
Suta said: Listen, best of sages, to the auspicious story of Harishvara, whereby Vishnu obtained Sudarshana from Shankara long ago.
At a certain time very mighty demons arose; they oppressed the worlds and brought about the decline of dharma.
The gods, oppressed by those demons of great strength and valour, told their sorrow to Vishnu, protector of the immortals.
The gods said: "Have mercy, lord; we are sorely oppressed by the demons. Where shall we go, what shall we do? We have come to you, our refuge."
Suta said: Hearing these words of the grieving gods, Vishnu, remembering the lotus feet of Shiva, spoke.
Vishnu said: "I will accomplish your task, O gods, by worshipping Girisha; these enemies are very strong and must be conquered with effort."

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, fourth book, the Kotirudra Samhita, chapter 35: the description of Shiva's thousand names. Suta said: Listen, best of sages, to that by which Maheshvara was pleased; I shall tell you today the thousand names of Shiva.
Friend of Kubera, Shrikantha, highest of the world's classes, the gentle; knowable in samadhi, bearer of the bow, the blue-throated, wielder of the axe;
Dhurjati of the matted locks, Khandaparashu of the broken axe, with parts and without parts, the sinless; beyond time, support of all, pale in hue, the gracious, the dancer;
The full, the fulfiller, the holy, the tender, the fair-eyed; lover of the Sama chants, the gentle, of holy fame, free of affliction;
Swift as the mind, maker of holy fords, the matted-haired, lord of life; ender of life, the eternal, whose seed is gold, giver of wealth;
The good goal, the good deed, accomplishment, of noble birth, a thorn to the wicked; bearer of the crescent, who has become Mahakala, devoted to truth;
Doer of the world's welfare, abode of happiness beyond the world; reviver of the moon, the ruler, hidden from the world, the great sovereign;
Kinsman of the world, lord of the world, the grateful, adorned with fame; the undecaying, the imperishable, the beloved, best of all who bear weapons;
Full of radiance, bearer of splendour, leader of the worlds, subtle as an atom; of pure smile, serene of soul, hard to conquer, hard to transgress;
Made of light, lord of the universe, the formless, lord of the waters; player of the gourd-lute, of great wrath, sorrowless, destroyer of sorrow;
Protector of the three worlds, lord of the three worlds, the purity of all, Adhokshaja; the god whose marks are unmanifest, manifest and unmanifest, lord of the people;
Of excellent conduct, of excellent qualities, the essence, rich in honour, Maya the builder; Brahma, Vishnu, protector of creatures, the swan, of swan's gait, the bird;
The wide-eyed, hunter of the deer, lord of the gods, who scorches the sun; abode of dharma, field of forbearance, the blessed one, piercer of Bhaga's eyes;
The ordainer, the disposer, the supporter, the creator, the destroyer, the four-faced; dweller on Kailasa's peak, dweller in all, the ever-moving;
Hiranyagarbha, Druhina, protector of beings and lord of the earth; the true yogi, knower of yoga, the yogi, giver of boons, dear to brahmins;
Dear to the gods, lord of the gods, knower of the gods, who thinks of the gods; the odd-eyed, the wide-eyed, giver of dharma, increaser of dharma;
Free of possessiveness, free of ego, free of delusion, free of harm; destroyer of pride, giver of pride, the proud, who turns all the seasons;
Conqueror of thousands, of a thousand rays, affectionate by nature and generous; lord of past, future and present, the source, destroyer of prosperity;
Wealth and non-wealth, the great treasury, skilled solely in the work of others; free of thorns, maker of bliss, without guile, crusher of guile;
Endowed with goodness, the sattvic, of true fame, who gave the scriptures out of affection; the unshaken, appreciator of virtue, of many selves, doer of many deeds;
The well pleased, the fair-faced, the subtle, the easily won, the southern breeze; borne on Nandi's shoulders, the bearer of burdens, the manifest, increaser of love;
The unconquered, the being of all, Govinda, borne on goodness; unsupported, self-supported, the perfected, of pure form, rich in fame;
Bearer of the boar's tusk, the horned, the mighty, the one leader; revealer of scripture, possessed of scripture, the one kinsman, doer of many things;
The fierce, Pashupati, Tarkshya, who loves his devotees, scorcher of foes; the giver, the merciful, the skilful, of the braided locks, chastiser of Kama;
Fond of Shri, of auspicious undertaking, peaceful and blessed, the even, fame itself; lying on the earth, the ornament, prosperity, maker of beings, sustainer of beings;
The unshakable, embodiment of devotion, slayer of Death, the blue-red one; of true vows, the great renouncer, ever devoted to peace;
Living for the good of others, giver of boons, the dispassionate, the expert; giver of good, doer of good, of auspicious name, goodness itself;
Unsought, beyond qualities, the witness, the non-doer, golden in lustre; good by nature, the impartial, slayer of enemies, destroyer of obstacles;
Crested, armoured, bearing the trident, matted-haired, shaven-headed, wearing earrings; deathless, all-seeing, the lion, mass of radiance, the great jewel;
The countless, of immeasurable self, the valiant, knower of valour; the knowable, whose nature is freedom from bonds, lord of sages high and low;
The unsurpassed, the unassailable, sweet and pleasing to behold; lord of the gods, the refuge, the all, the Word-Brahman, the goal of the good;
On the side of Time, Death of Death, who wears Vasuki as a bracelet; the great archer, sustainer of the earth, stainless, unfettered;
Jewel of the sky, the sun, the blessed, giver of success, means of success; enveloped on all sides, worthy of praise, broad-chested, mighty-armed;
Source of all, free of fear, dear to Nara and Narayana; untainted, whose self is beyond the manifold world, without defect, destroyer of defects;
Dwelling in the cremation ground, the subtle, abiding in the cremation ground, Maheshvara; maker of the world, lord of beasts, the great doer, the great medicine;
Worthy of hymns, fond of hymns, the praiser, embodied as Vyasa, unrestrained; the faultless means, treasury of knowledge, lover of rasa;
Of tranquil intellect, the unimpaired, the gatherer, ever beautiful; foremost in wearing the tiger-skin, lord of the earth, Shakalya, lord of the night;
Teacher of the highest truth, Datta, the sage, kind to those who depend on him; Soma, knower of rasa, giver of rasa, the support of all beings.
Thus Hari praised Hara with a thousand names; he entreated Shambhu and worshipped him with lotuses.
Then Shambhu, in play, did a deed, O brahmins, most wonderful and delightful; hear it with attention.
The deliverer, lord of cattle, the protector, reached by knowledge, the ancient; right conduct, good conduct, pure of soul, Soma, delighting in Soma, the happy;
Drinker of Soma, drinker of nectar, the gentle, of great energy, of great splendour; made of radiance, made of nectar, made of food, lord of ambrosia;
Who has no enemy, the light, the honoured, bearer of oblations; maker of the world, maker of the Vedas, author of the sutras, the eternal;
The great sage and teacher Kapila, light of the universe, the three-eyed; Pinaka in hand, god on earth, giver of well-being, maker of well-being, the wise;
Abode of the creator, maker of abodes, the all-pervading, perceived in all; creator of Brahma, creator of the universe, creation itself, fond of karnikara flowers, the seer;
Shakha, Vishakha, Goshakha, Shiva, the unsurpassed physician; whose water is the flood of the Ganga, the auspicious, the abundant, the architect, the steady;
Shri Vishnu said: Shiva, Hara, Mrida, Rudra, Pushkara, the flower-eyed; reached by seekers, of good conduct, Sharva, Shambhu, Maheshvara;
Self-conquered, self-controlled, charioteer of the vehicle of beings; attended by his hosts, whose body is the hosts, of fair fame, dispeller of doubts;
God of desire, guardian of desires, whose body is smeared with ash; fond of ash, lying on ash, the desiring, the lovely, author of the Agamas;
The turning cycle, of unreturning self, a heap of dharma, Sadashiva; stainless, four-armed, hard to dwell with, hard to approach;
Hard to obtain, hard to reach, the fortress, skilled in all weapons; abode of inner yoga, the good thread, increaser of the thread of lineage;
Of auspicious limbs, the deer of the world, lord of the universe, Janardana; purifier by ash, Meru, the vigorous, of pure form;
Unattainable, yet attainable by the good, who took the form of a monkey-servant; of golden seed, the ancient, taker of foes' lives, the mighty;
The great lake, the great abyss, praised by hosts of siddhas and gods; clothed in tiger-skin, wearing serpents, the great being, the great treasure;
Eater of nectar, of immortal body, Panchajanya, the tempest; abiding in the twenty-five principles, the Parijata tree, the high and the low;
Easy to reach, of good vows, the hero, treasury of Brahman and the Veda, the treasure; teacher of the classes and stages of life, the student, conqueror of foes, scorcher of foes;
The hermitage, the ascetic, the lean, the wise, lord of the mountains; the standard of knowledge, hard to know, Suparna, borne on the wind;
Crowned with the moon, moon-crested, the universe, lord of the all-sustaining earth; the distilled essence of Vedanta, the skull-bearer, the blue-red one;
Bearer of the bow, the science of archery, a heap of virtues, a mine of virtues; the true, devoted to truth, never downcast, whose body is dharma, the means of dharma;
Of endless vision, bliss, the rod of punishment, the subduer, self-restraint; worthy of salutation, of great maya, skilled in the making of the universe;
Free of passion, of disciplined self, the ascetic, sustainer of beings; in the guise of a madman, the hidden, conqueror of desire, dear to Ajita;
Auspicious by nature, the able, lord of the creatures of all worlds; the swift, the deliverer, the wise, primal matter, the lord, the imperishable;
Guardian of the world, of hidden self, beginning of the kalpa, lotus-eyed; knower of the true meaning of Veda and shastra, beyond rule, the steady refuge;
The moon, the sun, Saturn, Ketu, of excellent form, coral-hued; won by devotion, the supreme Brahman, who loosed the arrow at the deer, the sinless;
The mountain, dwelling on the mountain, the beloved, the supreme self, teacher of the world; abode of all actions, the content, the auspicious, surrounded by auspiciousness;
Of great austerity, of long austerity, the most vast, the ancient, the fixed; the day, the year, pervasion, the measure, the supreme austerity;
Maker of the year, known through mantras, all-seeing; the unborn, lord of all, the perfected, of great seed, of great strength;
The yogi, the fit, of great energy, accomplishment, the beginning of all, the ungraspable; Vasu, of generous mind, the true, remover of all sins, Hara;
Support of meditation, the unlimited, husband of Gauri, lord of the ganas; of eight forms, whose form is the universe, the means to the three aims of life and to heaven;
Shining with good fame, the glorious, whose limbs are the Vedas, knower of the Veda, the sage; the radiant, food, the enjoyer, lord of the world, hard to hold;
The immortal, the eternal, the peaceful, arrow in hand, the valorous; bearer of the water-pot, the archer, beyond the reach of speech and mind;
Beyond the senses, of great maya, dwelling in all, the crossroads; the yogi of time, the great sound, of great zeal, of great strength;
Of great intellect, of great valour, who moves among spirits, Purandara; who roams by night, who moves among ghosts, of great power, of great splendour;
Of indescribable form, the glorious, teacher of all, swift as the mind; of great learning, free of great maya, of controlled self, the fixed and the unfixed;
Bearer of vigour, energy and splendour, the father, ruler of all; lover of dance, ever dancing, of luminous self, the illuminator;
Of clear syllables, the wise, the mantra, the equal, the flood of essence; maker of the beginning of the ages, the turning of the ages, the profound, who rides the bull;
The desired, the undistinguished, dear to the cultured, easy to reach, purifier of the essence; in the form of a holy ford, named as a ford, seen at the fords, giver of holy fords;
Treasury of the waters, the foundation, the invincible, knower of the time for victory; the established, knower of the means of knowledge, with golden armour, Hari;
The liberator, the host of gods, lord of knowledge, resting in the bindu; child-formed, not mad with strength, the unchanging, the unfathomable, Guha;
Reached by knowledge, of firm wisdom, god of gods, the three-eyed; Vamadeva, Mahadeva, the skilful, the master, the firm;
The instrument, the cause, the doer, releaser from all bonds; resolve, the ordering, giver of place, first-born of the world;
Giver of the guru, the graceful, the undivided, whose self is being, established in the self; lord of heroes, Virabhadra, master of the hero's posture, Virat;
Crest-jewel of heroes, the knower, consciousness and bliss, bearer of the river; upholder of command, bearer of the trident, Shipivishta, abode of good;
The Valakhilya, of the great bow, of fierce rays, the deaf, the sky-goer; the delightful, the good refuge, Subrahmanya, lord of ambrosia;
Maghavan, Kaushika, rich in cattle, the cessation, the means of all; with an eye in his forehead, whose body is the universe, the essence, bearer of the wheel of samsara;
Whose rod never fails, the impartial, the golden, of brahmic lustre; the highest truth, the supreme, master of maya, Shambara, tiger-eyed;
Lustre, Viranchi, kinsman of heaven, lord of speech, lord of the day; Ravi, Virochana, Skanda, the ruler, Yama son of Vivasvat;
Reason, of lofty fame, full of affection, conqueror of foes; lord of Kailasa, the beloved, Savitri, sun-eyed;
Most learned, free of fear, sustainer of the universe, the unobstructed; eternal, of constant auspiciousness, the hearing and singing of whom is holy;
Far-hearing, all-enduring, worthy of meditation, destroyer of bad dreams; the deliverer, slayer of evil deeds, to be known, the unbearable, the unborn;
Of universal form, the odd-eyed, lord of speech, purest of the pure; in accord with all means of knowledge, bull-bannered, riding the bull;
Without beginning, the earth and the atmosphere, Lakshmi, the crowned, lord of the thirty gods; protector of the universe, maker of the universe, the great hero, with lovely armlets;
The begetter, origin of the birth of beings, the affectionate, the prudent, the husband; Vasishtha, Kashyapa, Bhanu, the terrible, of terrible valour;
The Pranava, walking the good path, the great treasury, of great wealth; lord of birth, Mahadeva, master of all the Agamas;
Truth, knower of truth, the one self, the all-pervading, ornament of the universe; the seer, the brahmin, beyond lordship, birth, death and old age;
Source of the five sacrifices, lord of the universe, of spotless rising; self-born, without beginning or end, the affectionate, sustainer of the world of devotees;
Beloved of Gayatri, the tall, dwelling-place of the universe, maker of light; the child, delighting in the mountain, the emperor, Sushena, slayer of the gods' foes;
The unfailing, Arishtanemi, Kumuda, free of fever; self-luminous, light of the body, light of the self, the unwavering;
The tawny, tawny-bearded, with an eye in the forehead, whose body is the three Vedas; mass of knowledge, of great wisdom, origin of the universe, the dissolution;
Bhaga, Vivasvat, Aditya, gone beyond yoga, lord of heaven; of auspicious qualities and names, destroyer of sin, holy to behold;
Of noble fame, the energetic, the true yogi, made of being and non-being; garlanded with stars, lord of heaven, resting in the Svadhishthana centre;
Isha, bearer of Pinaka, bearer of the khatvanga, of wondrous garb, the ancient; remover of darkness, the great yogi, the protector, Brahma, Dhurjati;
The pure, remover of sin, the Manipura centre, moving in the sky; seated in the lotus of the heart, Shakra, the peaceful, Vrishakapi;
The hot, lord of the house, Krishna, the capable, destroyer of misfortune; enemy of adharma, the unknowable, Puruhuta, widely renowned;
Womb of Brahman, of vast womb, the cow of dharma, source of wealth; seeker of the world's good, Sugata, the youth, the coming of welfare;
Golden-hued, the luminous, delighting in many beings, the sound; the passionless, presiding over the eyes, Vishvamitra, lord of wealth;
Light of Brahman, abode of wealth, the great light, the unsurpassed; the grandfather, Matarishvan, the wind, wearing a necklace of serpents;
Pulastya, Pulaha, Agastya, Jatukarnya, Parashara; unveiled and unhindered, son of Viranchi, Vishtarashravas;
Self-born, Aniruddha, Atri, embodiment of knowledge, of great fame; foremost of the world's heroes, the hero, the fierce, of true valour;
Adorned with serpents, the great kalpa, the wish-granting tree, bearer of the crescent; the adorner, the immovable, the shining, exalted in valour;
Lord of life and of sound, the swift, the leaping, whose charioteer is fire; the unattached, the guest, crusher of Shakra, seated on a tree;
Famed for wealth, bearer of oblations, the glowing, who feeds the universe; to be repeated in japa, queller of old age and the rest, red of nature, Tanunapat;
Death of Death, clad in hide, the fortunate, whose essence is Om; the unbound, the Person, the one to be served, Durvasas, chastiser of the cities;
Of mighty horses, source of the sky, of fine form, slayer of darkness; summer heat, the scorcher, the cloud, fair-eyed, conqueror of enemy cities;
The pleasant breeze, the well-perfected, the fragrant, of the nature of the cool season; spring, Madhava, summer, the rainy month, bearer of seed;
Angiras, the teacher, Atreya, the spotless, bearer of the universe; the purifier, of good mind, the learned, versed in the three Vedas, of excellent mount;
Mind, intellect and ego, knower of the field, guardian of the field; Jamadagni, treasury of strength, Vigala, Vishvagalava;
Aghora, the unsurpassed, the sacrifice, the best, giver of the highest good; the mountain, white as jasmine against the sky, foe of the danavas, subduer of enemies;
Father of the night, the lovely, free of thorns, who bears the world's thorns; of the four Vedas, of four states, the clever, fond of the clever;
The sacred tradition and its whole collection, the god of holy fords, abode of Shiva; of many forms, of great form, of all forms, the moving and the unmoving;
Maker of right order, the just, reached by reasoning, the stainless; thousand-headed, lord of the gods, breaker of all weapons;
The shaven, the misshapen, the valiant, the staff-bearer, the restrained, highest in virtue; tawny-eyed, overseer of people, blue-necked, free of disease;
Thousand-armed, lord of all, the refuge, upholder of all worlds; seated on the lotus, the supreme light, giver of the fruit of tradition;
Of divine weapons, father of Skanda, the most exalted, higher than the highest; without beginning, middle or end, Girisha, husband of Girija;
Lotus-wombed, of great womb, womb of the universe, the discerning; knower of high and low, giver of boons, the most excellent, of mighty voice;
Teacher of gods and asuras, the god, saluted by gods and asuras; great friend of gods and asuras, great lord of gods and asuras;
Lord of gods and asuras, the divine, great refuge of gods and asuras; made of the god of gods, the unthinkable, self-born as the god of gods;
Source of the real, tiger among asuras, lion among gods, the sun; best of those who go before the wise, highest of the highest of all gods;
Delighting in the knowledge of Shiva, the glorious, fond of the peacock and of Shriparvata; thunderbolt in hand, of the perfect sword, feller of Narasimha;
The celibate, moving through the worlds, walking in dharma, lord of wealth; Nandi, Nandishvara, the endless, keeping the vow of nakedness, the pure;
Presiding over the linga, over the gods and over yoga, bringer of the ages; of his own dharma, gone to heaven, the note of heaven, whose voice is made of musical notes;
Lord of Bana, maker of the seed, doer of dharma, source of dharma; hypocrisy, greed, knower of wealth, Shambhu, great lord of all beings;
Dwelling in the cremation ground, the three-eyed, the bridge, of incomparable form; of clear light beyond the world, Tryambaka, adorned with serpents;
Foe of Andhaka, hater of Daksha's sacrifice, who struck down Vishnu's neck; free of faults, of imperishable qualities, foe of Daksha, breaker of Pushan's teeth;
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, fourth book, the Kotirudra Samhita, chapter 36: the description of the fruit of the hymn of Shiva's thousand names. Suta said: Hearing the divine hymn of a thousand names composed by Vishnu, adorned with the highest names, Maheshvara was pleased.
Shankara said: "I know all that your mind desires, Hari — above all the work of the gods, for you are devoted to the gods' work.
For the success of the gods' work and the destruction of the demons, I give you, as a refuge, the beautiful discus named Sudarshana.
The form you have seen, which brings happiness to all worlds, I have assumed for your good, lord of gods; meditate on it steadily.
Remembered on the battlefield, it destroys the sorrow of the gods. This discus, this form, this thousand names —
for those who always hear them with devotion there will be unfailing fulfilment of all desires, by my grace, O you of good vows."
Suta said: Having said this, he gave the discus Sudarshana, radiant as ten thousand suns, sprung from his own foot, destroyer of all enemies.
Vishnu, having duly consecrated it, received it facing north; then, bowing to Mahadeva, Vishnu spoke.
Vishnu said: "Tell me, God, lord, Shankara of the world, what I should meditate upon and recite for the destruction of sorrows."
Suta said: Asked thus by him, Shiva, pleased and gracious of mind, spoke to Vishnu, the helper of the gods.
Shiva said: "Hari, meditate on my form for the quelling of all misfortunes; recite the thousand names for the destruction of many sorrows.
To test Hari, the lord Maheshvara, ruler of the worlds, then hid one lotus among the lotuses.
Always bear my discus with care, Vishnu, for the fulfilment of every wish; it is the best of all discuses.
Others too who recite it or have it recited daily — sorrow will not come to them even in dreams; of this there is no doubt.
When trouble from kings befalls, if a man performs a hundred recitations, complete with its subsidiary parts and according to rule, he gains welfare.
This removes disease, bestows learning and wealth, is supreme, grants all desires, is holy, and always gives devotion to Shiva.
Whatever excellent fruit men aim at in reciting it here, they will obtain that fruit, true and excellent; there is no doubt.
Whoever rises at dawn, performs my worship and recites it daily before me — success is not far from him.
He gains every worldly success, fulfilling all desires, and in the end attains the liberation of union with me; there is no doubt."
Suta said: Having spoken thus to Vishnu, Shankara, pleased in mind, touched him with both hands, and Girisha spoke again.
Shiva said: "I am the giver of boons, best of gods; choose boons as you wish. Truly I am won over by your devotion and by this hymn, O you of good vows."
Suta said: Addressed thus by the god of gods, Vishnu bowed to him and, most gladdened, spoke with folded hands.
Among those thousand lotuses one was then missing, and Vishnu was distressed in his worship of Shiva.
Vishnu said: "As grace is now shown by you, lord, beyond what is shown to others, so let it be shown especially, from your compassion, O master:
devotion to you, Mahadeva — be gracious, that is the best boon. I want nothing else, lord, for your devotees know no suffering."
Suta said: Hearing his words, Bhava, full of compassion, touched his body, and the moon-crested one said:
Shiva said: "May your devotion to me, Hari, be ever unfailing; may you always be worthy of salutation and worship in the world, even by the gods.
Your name Vishvambhara will be supreme, removing all sins — no doubt of it — by my grace, best of gods."
Suta said: Having said this, Rudra, lord of all gods, the master, vanished right there as Vishnu looked on, O lords of sages.
The blessed Janardana too, having obtained that auspicious discus at Shankara's word, rejoiced greatly in his heart.
Meditating on Shambhu, he recited this hymn constantly, taught it, and imparted it to devotees.
Thus I have told what you asked, which removes the sins of those who hear it. What else, O best ones, do you wish to ask now?
He thought in his heart: "Where has the lotus gone? Let it go, and welcome; is not my eye a lotus?"
Resolving thus, he plucked out his eye, relying on the one who supports all beings, and with it worshipped and praised him devoutly.
Then Hara, the teacher of the world, seeing Hari so praising him and in that state, appeared, crying "Do not, do not!"
Maheshvara swiftly descended from the circle of the earthen image, his own linga that Hari had consecrated.
Bowing to Shambhu, in the form described, risen as a mass of radiance, and standing before him, Vishnu praised him especially.
Then Mahadeva, pleased and as if smiling, looking with compassion at Vishnu standing with folded hands, spoke.
Salutations to Shri Ganesha.
Salutations to Shri Gauri and Shankara.

The glorious Shiva Mahapurana, fourth book, the Kotirudra Samhita, chapter 37: the account of the Shaiva devotion of gods, sages and kings. The sages said: "Suta, Suta, most fortunate one, you are wise, O man of good vows; tell us again in detail the deeds of Shiva alone.
Arundhati the great chaste woman, Lopamudra, and Ahalya the wife of Gautama were worshippers of Shiva.
Durvasas, Kaushika, Shakti, Dadhichi and Gautama, Kanada, Bhargava, Jiva and Vaishampayana —
all these sages are held to be worshippers of Shiva; so too Parashara and Vyasa were ever devoted to Shiva's worship.
Upamanyu was a great devotee of Shiva, the supreme self; Yajnavalkya was a great Shaiva, and Jaimini and Garga too.
Shuka, Shaunaka and others were worshippers of Shankara; and there are many other sages as well, O best of sages.
Aditi, mother of the gods, together with her daughters-in-law, devoted in love, daily performed the earthen worship of Shiva with affection.
Shakra and the other world-guardians, the Vasus and the gods, the Maharajika gods and the Sadhyas were worshippers of Shiva.
The gandharvas, kinnaras and other demigods were worshippers of Shiva; so too the great-souled asuras are held to be worshippers of Shiva.
The daitya Hiranyakashipu, with his younger brother and his sons, O sage, worshipped Shiva daily, as did Virochana and Bali.
Bana is remembered as a great Shaiva, as are the sons of Hiranyaksha; Vrishaparvan and Danu, dear one, and the danavas were worshippers of Shiva.
The ancient kings, sages and gods, too, worshipped that very best of gods."
Shesha, Vasuki, Takshaka and other great serpents were devotees of Shiva, as were Garuda and the other birds.
Both the sun and moon gods, founders of dynasties on earth, were ever devoted to the service of Shiva together with their descendants, O lord of sages.
The Manus too, headed by Svayambhuva, performed the worship of Shiva especially, wearing Shiva's garb, O sage.
Priyavrata and his sons, the son of Uttanapada, and the kings of their lines were worshippers of Shiva.
Dhruva, Rishabha, Bharata, the nine yogis and their other brothers were worshippers of Shiva.
The sons of Vaivasvata, Tarkshya, and the kings headed by Ikshvaku were devoted to Shiva's worship and always enjoyed happiness.
Kakutstha, Mandhatri, Sagara the best of Shaivas, Muchukunda, Harishchandra and Kalmashapada too,
Bhagiratha and many other excellent kings are to be known as worshippers of Shiva who wore Shiva's garb.
The great king Khatvanga, a helper of the gods, always worshipped the earthen image of Shiva according to rule.
His son Dilipa always worshipped Shiva; his son Raghu, a Shaiva, worshipped Shiva with great love.
Suta said: "Well asked, best of sages; listen, I will tell you the delightful deeds of Shankara, which give enjoyment and liberation to those who hear them.
His son Aja, a worshipper of Shiva, fought righteously; from him was born Dasharatha, a great king above all.
For the sake of a son, Dasharatha especially worshipped the earthen image of Shiva at the command of the sage Vasishtha.
That best of kings, devoted to Bhava, also performed the sacrifice for a son, having received the command of the sage Rishyashringa.
His beloved Kausalya, as Rishyashringa directed, joyfully worshipped the earthen image of Shankara to obtain a son.
Sumitra and Kaikeyi, the king's beloved, also lovingly worshipped Shiva to obtain good sons, O best of sages.
By Shiva's grace they obtained auspicious sons, of great might, heroic and devoted to the right path, O sage.
Then, by Shiva's command, Hari himself was born of the king through them, manifesting in four forms as the king's sons.
Kausalya's son was Rama, Sumitra's were Lakshmana and Shatrughna, and Kaikeyi's was Bharata — all of good vows.
Rama with his brothers always worshipped the earthen linga, wearing ash and rudraksha and following the Viraja rite.
The kings born in his line, with their followers, O sage, all worshipped the earthen linga of Shiva.
Long ago Narada asked the Grandsire this very thing, and he, pleased in mind, replied to Narada, best of sages.
The great king Sudyumna, son of Manu, was a Shaiva, O sage; through Shiva's curse, on account of his beloved, he became a woman along with his attendants.
